observations:
Torah LM2 #61 teaches a single unified philosophical argument: God is above time (and space), because time and space are functions of limited intellect and limited power respectively. The greater the שֵׂכֶל (intellect), the more time is annulled; the greater the כֹּחַ (power), the more space shrinks. The teaching uses two analogies — the dream (חֲלוֹם) to illustrate the intellect-time axis, and the powerful traveler (בַּעַל כֹּחַ) to illustrate the power-space axis — and culminates in the case of מָשִׁיחַ, whose future infinite intellect will annul all time since creation.

For a new package to be warranted, the spec requires 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language ('הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', 'כַּנַּ"ל') forming an independent domain. The entire text of Torah 61 contains no such language. The Rebbe's method here is philosophical argumentation and analogy, not the bechina-equating structure that generates packages.

The potential conceptual clusters one could identify are:
- {שֵׂכֶל, זְמַן, חֲלוֹם, כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה, מָשִׁיחַ} — the intellect-time axis
- {כֹּחַ, מָקוֹם, בַּעַל כֹּחַ, חֲלוּשֵׁי כֹּחַ} — the power-space axis

But these clusters are bound together by causal-proportional logic (eitza), not by shared essential nature (bechina). The Rebbe is not saying that שֵׂכֶל IS זְמַן or that they share the same essential nature; he is saying that שֵׂכֶל inversely determines the magnitude of זְמַן. Similarly, כֹּחַ inversely determines the magnitude of מָקוֹם. These are eitza relationships. Grouping them into packages on the basis of eitza connections would violate the core rule: 'Built on bechinas only — packages are formed from bechina-connected nodes, not eitza edges.'

No new packages are proposed.
